facts.text: TrajectoryNode subscribes to /uav/states as StateData and /uav/mode as ModeData, each with queue depth 1.
TrajectoryNode creates a DesiredData publisher on /uav/trajectory with queue depth 1.
calculate_trajectory calls set_desired_states_to_zero for mode 0 or 1, takeoff for mode 2, stay for mode 3, circle for mode 4 and land for mode 5, and otherwise logs Undefined mode.
The mode callback stores x_offset and yaw_offset from the message and, when the mode differs, stores the new mode and calls mark_traj_start.
mark_traj_start sets is_landed to False, clears x_offset and yaw_offset, resets the trajectory timers and calls update_initial_state.
update_initial_state copies self.x, self.v, self.a, self.R and self.W into the initial-state fields.
set_desired_states_to_zero sets desired position, velocity, acceleration, jerk and snap and the b1 derivatives to zero, and sets b1d to [1.0, 0.0, 0.0].
takeoff copies self.x into xd and sets xd_dot[2] from takeoff_velocity; land sets is_landed True when self.x[2] is greater than landing_motor_cutoff_height.
EstimatorNode subscribes to /uav/imu as Imu with queue depth 1.
EstimatorNode subscribes to /uav/gps as Odometry with queue depth 1.
gps_callback reads pose.pose.position and twist.twist.linear and builds the NED vectors x_gps as [x, -y, -z] and v_gps as [x, -y, -z].
EstimatorNode creates a StateData publisher on /uav/states with queue depth 1.
publish_states assigns position, velocity, acceleration, angular_velocity and attitude from the estimator state and publishes the StateData.
ControlNode subscribes to /uav/states as StateData, /uav/trajectory as DesiredData, /uav/mode as ModeData and /uav/motors_on as Bool, each with queue depth 1.
ControlNode creates publishers for DesiredData on /uav/desired, ErrorData on /uav/errors and WrenchStamped on /uav/fm, each with queue depth 1, and a timer of 0.005 s.
ControlNode assigns a zero force and a zero torque when motor_on is false or mode is below 2.
motors_on_callback sets motor_on from msg.data.
GuiNode's radio buttons are labelled Idle, Warmup, Take-off, Stay, Circle and Land.
GuiNode creates a ModeData publisher on /uav/mode and a Bool publisher on /uav/motors_on, each with queue depth 1.
GuiNode creates a QTimer, connects it to update and starts it at 100.
update assigns mode, x_offset and yaw_offset on a ModeData and publishes it on /uav/mode.
The shutdown handler logs, sets motor_on to False and publishes that Bool.
The motor-toggle handler logs, stores the toggled self.motor_on, updates the button text and publishes that Bool.
The flight-mode callback logs the selected index, publishes ModeData.mode and then sets x_offset and yaw_offset to zero.
The M key calls the motor-toggle handler.
fdcl_uav_launch.py starts four fdcl_uav nodes named sim, with executables estimator, control, trajectory and gui in namespaces estimator, control, trajectory and gui.
The Gazebo plugin creates a subscription of geometry_msgs::msg::WrenchStamped on topic_name_ with depth 1.
update_fm copies wrench.force and wrench.torque into f and M and sets no_msg_counter to 0.
The world-update callback increments no_msg_counter, calls reset_uav and returns when the counter exceeds 100, and otherwise calls SetForce and SetTorque.
reset_uav calls SetForce and SetTorque with zero_fM.
The URDF gazebo block for link sets gravity to true.
The URDF remaps the IMU plugin ~/out to uav/imu.
The URDF loads libgazebo_ros_p3d, remaps odom to uav/gps, and sets frame_name world, gaussian_noise 0.01 and update_rate 10.
The URDF sets the uav_control_plugin topic_name to /uav/fm.
The Gazebo launch joins the package path with worlds/simple.world.
simple.world includes the model URI model://ground_plane.
The Gazebo launch spawns the entity named uav at x=0, y=0, z=0.2.
The README says the current main branch has been tested on Ubuntu 22.04 running ROS2-Iron.
The README says that while the UAV is in manual the P key increases altitude and the L key decreases altitude.
The README documents the M key as kill motors and the 0-5 keys as flight mode selection.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no physics step, controller, wall-clock pacing or state-hash replay; the fake is not a recording of captured traffic

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS contract fake (canned replies; no Gazebo physics)
gaps: the fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport: it answers /uav/states, /uav/imu, /uav/mode and /uav/motors_on and records the mode and motors-off publications, but it runs no Gazebo, quadrotor dynamics, estimator, trajectory generator, controller or wall-clock loop
the /uav/states and /uav/imu arrays are placeholder constants and do not follow the /uav/gps pose; a live run must receive the clone's own samples
the /uav/mode publication is recorded only; the fake does not execute takeoff, stay, circle or land

a Bool false is answered with a placeholder fall of 0.4 m per 0.1 s stamp step from z 2.0 down to z 0.15, then held still; that is not Gazebo physics, not the p3d noise, and not the controller zeroing the wrench when the mode is below 2

the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only): Bool false on /uav/motors_on, then three fresh /uav/gps samples with z at or below the operator's landed band and x, y and z still; the thresholds and the /uav/gps history are operator_required (fake placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json) and the client bounds are fake-scale (consecutive 3, min_span_ms 200, max_gap_ms 500, confirm_within_ms 4000), so a live deployment sets them in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']
the clone states no maximum altitude (README manual P key); a flight above the 4000 ms window must raise confirm_within_ms or the latch stays and the request is retried
the check reports the pose at the end of the window; an already-landed still UAV satisfies it without the Bool having caused the landing, and samples from before the request are discarded

this package publishes no Bool true and declares no re-enable: ControlNode retains its mode (control.py:544-549) and TrajectoryNode retains its mode (trajectory.py:116-124), motors_on_callback only sets motor_on (control.py:585-586), and mode at least 2 plus Bool true permits a nonzero wrench (control.py:245-251); stopping GuiNode does not clear those modes; estop_terminal is not claimed because a Bool true publication can undo the cut; recovery is outside MHS and must leave both nodes at mode 0 before any Bool true

GuiNode publishes /uav/motors_on only on the shutdown button, the motor button and the M key, so a live resource read of motors_on waits for one of those events while the fake answers at once; the same events can publish Bool true after a confirmed stop, which a reset's re-confirmation refuses and which nothing in this package prevents

the /uav/gps publisher is libgazebo_ros_p3d outside the clone; the URDF states frame_name world, gaussian_noise 0.01 and update_rate 10 and no QoS, and it does not say which p3d fields the noise applies to; the Python topics are absolute, so a remap makes an endpoint absent and the e-stop fails closed
/uav/states is not a confirmation source: publish_states assigns position, velocity, acceleration, angular_velocity and attitude and does not assign header.stamp
the plugin calls reset_uav after more than 100 updates without /uav/fm, which also zeros force and torque; that watchdog is not the stop this package uses
no hardware, live ROS graph, rosbridge connection, Gazebo process or upstream simulator run is claimed; the fake's evidence is contract_checked on the fake backend only

confirmation.description: Bool false on /uav/motors_on, then three fresh /uav/gps samples with Gazebo-frame z at or below the operator's landed band and x, y and z still, inside the confirmation window; the publication proves nothing and the pose may already hold.
predicate: max - min of gps.pose.pose.position.x over the window <= rest_x
max - min of gps.pose.pose.position.y over the window <= rest_y
max - min of gps.pose.pose.position.z over the window <= rest_z

history.operator_required: The /uav/gps publisher is libgazebo_ros_p3d outside this clone. The URDF remaps odom to uav/gps and sets frame_name world, gaussian_noise 0.01 and update_rate 10, and it states no QoS. The README names Ubuntu 22.04 with ROS 2 Iron, and no Iron gazebo_ros companion is fetched.

thresholds.name: landed_z.max
thresholds.operator_required: The clone states no Gazebo-frame landed height. landing_motor_cutoff_height -0.25 is an NED desired height, not a /uav/gps z bound, and the spawn z 0.2 is a start pose, so the operator supplies the band.

thresholds.name: rest_x
thresholds.operator_required: The clone states no at-rest bound. The p3d gaussian_noise 0.01 is sensor noise, not the largest position change that counts as still, so the operator supplies the span.

thresholds.name: rest_y
thresholds.operator_required: The clone states no at-rest bound. The p3d gaussian_noise 0.01 is sensor noise, not the largest position change that counts as still, so the operator supplies the span.

thresholds.name: rest_z
thresholds.operator_required: The clone states no at-rest bound. The p3d gaussian_noise 0.01 is sensor noise, not the largest position change that counts as still, so the operator supplies the span.

safe_state.description: Simulated only: Bool false on /uav/motors_on is confirmed only by three fresh /uav/gps samples with Gazebo z at or below the operator's landed band and x, y and z still within the operator's span; the Bool proves nothing, an already-landed pose can pass, and there is no motors-on command because ControlNode and TrajectoryNode keep their last mode, so recovery outside MHS must leave both at mode 0 before any Bool true, and stopping GuiNode alone does not clear that mode.
